To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mitochondrial genome of CD4 T cells in HIV-1 seropositives declines with time after seroconversion, but that the decline is dependent on the degree of immune activation, which is a major risk factor for HIV-1 infection.
the decline in mtDNA copy number in HIV-1 seropositive individuals is not associated with age, but is dependent on CD4+ T cell count and viral load.

the mitochondrial DNA content in T cells is decreased in HIV-1 seropositives compared to seronegative controls, that this decrease in mitochondrial DNA content is dependent on immune activation, and that this decrease in mtDNA content is associated with increased apoptosis of T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the mitochondrial DNA in HIV-1 infection and AIDS.
the effects of HIV-1 infection on the mitochondrial DNA content in peripheral blood CD4+ T cells.
the effects of the immune response on the mitochondrial DNA content of CD4 T cells in the context of HIV-1 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV-1 seroprevalence among MSM in China was still high, and HIV-1 serostatus was associated with a higher prevalence of STI and sexual risk behaviours among MSM in China.
the evidence of a link between HIV and mitochondrial dysfunction is still not clear.

the evidence is not yet sufficient to establish that the mitochondrial DNA content of T cells declines with HIV-1 seropositivity and/or HIV-1 infection and that this is dependent on immune activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immune activation in the HIV-1 serocorverters was associated with mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) decline in the CD8+ T cells, and the mtDNA decline in the CD4+ T cells was associated with the CD8+ mtDNA decline.

we found a mitochondrial DNA decline in T-cells of seroconverters, but not of HIV-1 positive long-term non-progressors, and that this decline was dependent on immune activation, as measured by the activation marker CD38 on T-cells.
mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is a biomarker of T cell activation and mitochondrial dysfunction, and that mtDNA is a predictor of HIV disease progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) decline may be an early event in T cell activation in HIV-1 infection and may be associated with immune activation.
mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) decline in T cells is not a consequence of HIV-1 infection per se, but rather is associated with the level of immune activation in the host.
mitochondrial dysfunction is a common feature of aging, and it is a major contributor to the decline in immune function that occurs with aging.
